note_sections.t: Assessment of a previously positive prostate biopsy alongside a steadily climbing PSA trajectory.

First brought to clinical attention for a PSA elevation in late 2022, this 70-year-old gentleman has a previously positive prostate biopsy bucket recording Gleason 3+4 pathology. He endures severe lower urinary tract symptoms, scoring 34 on the IPSS, which heavily disrupts his daily activities despite a lack of prior surgical interventions. A retired postal worker who has never married, he resides alone with his adult daughter acting as primary contact and a longstanding friend listed as next of kin. His lifestyle includes cycling roughly 20 kilometres twice each week and drinking about five alcohol units weekly; he ceased smoking 29 pack-years ago back in 2007. Aside from a right knee arthroscopy in 2018 and a recent practice-nurse-administered influenza vaccine, his medical background remains clear. He explicitly denies unexplained weight loss, bone pain, or haematuria.

Normal DRE: The prostate measures symmetrically enlarged, presenting a smooth capsule devoid of palpable nodules or asymmetry. General examination remains unremarkable, characterised by stable vital signs and an absence of systemic illness or lymphadenopathy.
